Understanding whether you qualify should be simple, clear, and stress-free — that is exactly how we keep it at EZ Mortgage Broker. By combining federal support with state-based revenue exemptions, many first-time buyers can enter the Australian property market with significantly less upfront capital than traditionally required.
1. New & Expanded National Programs Making Home Ownership Possible

Key government initiatives have introduced lower genuine savings requirements, stamp duty waivers, and shared equity options that drastically shorten the time needed to save a deposit.

title: NDIS & SDA Property Investment Finance in Australia: The Complete Lending Guide
author: R BAKSHI
summary: Specialist Disability Accommodation (SDA) property investment under the NDIS offers projected 8%–14% gross rental yields. Learn how to secure non-bank, construction, and SMSF finance from specialist Australian lenders.
body: Specialist Disability Accommodation (SDA) property investment under the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) has become one of the most discussed wealth-creation strategies in Australia. Offering projected gross rental yields between 8% and 14% and stable, government-backed funding packages, SDA homes offer both strong financial returns and crucial, life-changing housing for Australians with significant disabilities.

⚡ Specialist Lending Notice: Traditional major retail banks frequently decline NDIS construction and investment loans due to specialized valuation methods, non-standard lease structures, and stringent building compliance codes. At EZ Mortgage Broker, we connect you directly with specialist non-bank and commercial lenders across Victoria, New South Wales, and Australia-wide.
1. What Is NDIS Specialist Disability Accommodation (SDA)?

Specialist Disability Accommodation refers to purpose-built, accessible housing tailored for NDIS participants who require specialized housing due to extreme functional impairment or very high support needs. The ecosystem involves six key stakeholders working together to fund, build, manage, and care for participants.

🏢
1. Private Investor / SMSF

Buys land, funds the build, and retains 100% property ownership.

🏗️
2. Registered SDA Builder

Constructs to strict NDIS Design Standards (HPS, Robust, Fully Accessible).

📋
3. Approved SDA Provider

Manages NDIA compliance, participant enrolment, and lease agreements.

🤝
4. SIL Care Provider

Delivers daily on-site 24/7 care and support to residents.

♿
5. NDIS Participant

Lives securely with funded SDA package & reasonable rent contribution (RRC).

🛡️
6. EZ Mortgage Broker

Structures non-bank, construction drawdowns, and SMSF loan facilities.
2. The Four SDA Design Categories & Yield Profiles

Lenders evaluate your borrowing risk and income shading based on the specific SDA design category of the property. Different categories cater to distinct participant requirements with varying yield outcomes:

SDA CategoryTarget NDIS ParticipantKey Architectural FeaturesYield Profile
High Physical Support (HPS)Very high support needs requiring ceiling hoists & 24/7 careEmergency power backup, home automation, ceiling hoist structural mounts, 1500mm circulationHighest (10%–14%)
Robust ConstructionComplex behavioral support & sensory managementHigh-impact wall linings, acoustic soundproofing, laminated safety glass, secure outdoor areasVery Strong (9%–12%)
Fully AccessibleSignificant physical disabilities (wheelchair users)Level thresholds, wide doorways, wheelchair-accessible kitchens & roll-in bathroomsStrong (8%–11%)
Improved LiveabilitySensory, intellectual, or cognitive impairmentsHigh visual contrast, clear lines of sight, luminance contrast fixturesModerate (7%–9%)
3. How Lenders Assess NDIS & SDA Loan Applications
When applying for an NDIS property loan, standard bank assessment calculators do not apply. Lenders focus on three critical underwriting criteria to evaluate serviceability and security value:

💰CRITERION A

Cash Flow & Income Shading

While an NDIS property may generate $80,000 to $120,000+ gross annual income, lenders shade rental income to standard market residential rent during the initial build and enrollment phase.

✓ Verifies personal income buffer during vacancy
📐CRITERION B

Valuation (Alternate Use Value)

Because SDA homes have specialized modifications, lenders value the home on an Alternate Use Value (what the property is worth if sold as a standard residential home to the open market).

✓ Valuation Gap: Covered by investor equity
📊CRITERION C

LVR Limits & SMSF Rules

Standard residential NDIS purchases qualify for up to 70%–80% LVR through specialist non-bank lenders. SMSF purchases qualify for up to 60%–70% LVR under an LRBA structure.

✓ 70%–80% Residential / 60%–70% SMSF
4. Purchasing NDIS Property Through SMSF

Self-Managed Super Funds (SMSFs) are a popular vehicle used by Australian investors to acquire SDA property due to substantial tax concessions. Super fund borrowing rules (LRBA) require a Single Part Contract structure or specialized funder solutions, minimum liquidity balances of $350k+, and strict adherence to arm's-length sole purpose test regulations. In accumulation phase, earnings are taxed at 15%, dropping to 0% in retirement pension phase.
5. Construction Loans for NDIS Builds: Progress Drawdown Stages

Financing the construction of an SDA home involves specific progress drawdown stages verified by bank quantity surveyors: Deposit & Base Stage (15%–20%), Frame Stage (20%), Lock-Up Stage (25%), Fixing Stage (20%), and Practical Completion & SDA Enrolment (15%–20%). Once final compliance certification is issued by an accredited SDA Assessor, the dwelling is formally enrolled with the NDIA.
6. Frequently Asked Questions (NDIS Property Finance)

Which lenders in Australia finance NDIS and SDA properties?

Major retail banks generally do not provide direct retail mortgages for private SDA builds. Financing is primarily provided by specialized non-bank lenders (e.g. La Trobe, Bluestone, RedZed, Firstmac), boutique credit unions, and commercial mortgage managers.

Is rental income guaranteed by the government?

No. While the SDA funding attached to the participant is government-funded through the NDIS, income depends on the property being enrolled and occupied by an eligible tenant. Investors must manage potential vacancy periods.

Can I refinance my existing residential equity to fund an NDIS deposit?

Yes. Many investors release equity from their owner-occupied home or standard investment portfolio to fund the required 20% to 30% deposit and closing costs.

title: Self-Employed Home Loans: The Ultimate Guide to Alt-Doc & Low-Doc Approvals
author: R BAKSHI
summary: Sole traders, contractors, and company directors: How to secure competitive home loan approvals with 1-year tax returns, bank statements, or ABN under 2 years.
body: Running your own business or working as an independent contractor in Australia is deeply rewarding, but traditional retail bank lending algorithms often penalize entrepreneurs. Standard retail bank credit models require two consecutive years of lodged personal and company tax returns, frequently penalizing business owners who utilize legitimate tax deductions, depreciation write-offs, or recent revenue growth.
1. What Are Alt-Doc (Alternative Documentation) Loans?

An Alt-Doc (Alternative Documentation) home loan is a specialist mortgage product designed for self-employed borrowers, freelancers, contractors, and company directors who have strong cash flow and serviceability but cannot supply two full financial years of finalized tax returns. Instead of relying purely on taxable income reported to the ATO, specialist lenders assess alternative financial documentation such as 6 to 12 months of business bank statements, quarterly Business Activity Statements (BAS), or an Accountant’s Declaration Letter.

Through our panel of over 50 Australian lenders, Alt-Doc loans allow borrowers to purchase residential homes, construct new builds, or secure commercial property with loan-to-value ratios (LVR) up to 80%–85% without paying extortionate interest rate penalties. Once two consecutive years of strong tax returns are lodged, EZ Mortgage Broker can seamlessly transition you back to prime retail interest rates with zero hassle.

📊
1-Year Tax Return Policy

Assess 100% of your latest financial year rather than averaging two past years.

💼
Bank Statement Verification

Verify true business turnover using 6–12 months of trading accounts.

🧾
Quarterly BAS Lending

Use ATO-verified GST turnover to prove consistent quarterly profitability.

✍️
Accountant's Declaration

Certified statement from your CPA confirming current annual net profit.

⏳
ABN Under 2 Years

Day-1 or 6-month ABN solutions for proven industry professionals.

🏢
Company Director Add-Backs

Add back depreciation, director super, and interest to maximize borrowing.
2. Borrowing with 1 Year of Tax Returns (Bypassing Bank Averaging)

A major bottleneck for growing businesses is the traditional banking rule of averaging your last two financial years. For instance, if your business earned $80,000 in Year 1 during startup phase and expanded to $180,000 in Year 2, a major bank will average your earnings at $130,000. This significantly restricts your purchasing power and prevents you from buying in competitive Australian property markets.

Specialist 1-year tax return lenders assess your full $180,000 latest income, recognizing your current trading reality. Furthermore, our brokers identify legitimate profit add-backs that retail branch managers frequently miss—including equipment depreciation, instant asset write-offs, voluntary director superannuation contributions, and one-off capital expenditures—which directly boosts your maximum borrowing capacity by up to $150,000 or more.
3. Applying with an ABN Registered Under 2 Years

If you recently transitioned from a full-time PAYG role to working as a self-employed sole trader or proprietary limited contractor in the same industry, major retail banks will routinely decline your application until you achieve a minimum 24-month trading history. This policy leaves many highly skilled Australian professionals locked out of home ownership despite earning higher gross revenue than their previous salaried roles.

EZ Mortgage Broker works with non-bank and tier-2 mortgage managers that provide Day-1 or 6-month ABN lending solutions. Provided you have demonstrated previous experience in your profession, ongoing client contracts, or a continuous line of work, we can secure competitive pre-approval for residential purchases and refinances across Melbourne, Sydney, and nationwide.
4. Frequently Asked Questions (Self-Employed Lending)

Are Alt-Doc interest rates much higher than standard bank rates?

Not significantly. Many tier-2 and non-bank lenders offer 1-year tax return and bank statement products priced within 0.30% to 0.70% of standard prime retail variable rates. The small rate variance is vastly outweighed by the ability to purchase property years earlier.

Can I buy an investment property or build a home under Alt-Doc?

Yes. Alt-Doc lending applies to owner-occupied homes, investment properties, vacant land, and progressive construction drawdowns for house-and-land packages across Victoria and Australia-wide.

title: How to Refinance and Save Thousands: The Complete Australian Mortgage Playbook

summary: Learn how switching lenders can lower your monthly repayments, unlock usable home equity, and secure cashback incentives across Australia.
body: With major banks constantly competing for quality borrowers, leaving your home loan on autopilot can cost you thousands of dollars in excess interest every single year. The 'loyalty tax' in Australian banking is real: lenders often reserve their sharpest interest rates for brand new customers while existing long-term borrowers remain on higher uncompetitive revert rates.
1. When Is the Right Time to Refinance Your Mortgage?

Refinancing is the process of replacing your current home loan with a new facility from either your existing lender or an alternative institution. A successful refinance should achieve at least one of four core objectives:

📉
Interest Rate Reduction

A 0.50% rate drop on a $650,000 mortgage saves over $3,250 annually.

💵
Lender Cashback Offers

🔒

🎯
Better Loan Features

Upgrade to 100% multiple offset accounts and fee-free redraw facilities.
2. Step-by-Step Australian Refinance Process

At EZ Mortgage Broker, we manage the entire refinancing lifecycle from beginning to end so you never have to waste hours on hold with bank call centers. We conduct a 360° health check on your current rate, order upfront bank valuations to verify your current equity, calculate your exact break-even timeline after discharge and government fees, and manage the lender discharge coordination directly.
3. Debt Consolidation: Cutting Monthly Living Outgoings

If you have accumulated car finance at 8%–12% interest, credit cards at 19%–22% interest, or personal loans, rolling these liabilities into a 6.00% home loan structure can slash your aggregate monthly cash outgoings by $800 to $1,500+ per month. We structure your consolidated debts with dedicated sub-accounts so you can pay them down rapidly without stretching them over a 30-year term.
4. Refinancing FAQs

How long does a refinance take to settle?

Typically 2 to 4 weeks from formal application to final settlement. We fast-track digital identity verification and digital title searches to minimize processing delays.

What upfront fees are involved in switching lenders?

Standard government title discharge and registration fees average $300 to $450, while outgoing lender discharge administration fees average $150 to $350. These are frequently covered entirely by incoming lender cashback rebates.

title: Understanding the Family Home Guarantee: Buy with Just a 2% Deposit
author: R BAKSHI
summary: Single parents and legal guardians can enter the Australian property market with as little as a 2% deposit without paying Lenders Mortgage Insurance.
body: For single parents, saving a traditional 20% home deposit while managing daily living expenses and childcare costs can feel nearly impossible. The Australian Government’s Family Home Guarantee (FHG), administered by Housing Australia, was created specifically to eliminate this hurdle and provide single parents and legal guardians a path into secure, long-term home ownership.
1. How the 2% Deposit Scheme Works

Under the Family Home Guarantee, eligible single parents with at least one dependent child can purchase a residential property with as little as a 2% genuine savings deposit. The Australian Government acts as a guarantor for up to 18% of the property's value, enabling borrowers to secure standard prime bank interest rates without paying Lenders Mortgage Insurance (LMI), saving between $15,000 and $35,000 upfront.

👨‍👧
Single Parents & Guardians

Open to mothers, fathers, and legal guardians with dependent children.

💵
Just 2% Deposit Needed

Save $12,000 deposit on a $600,000 family home rather than $120,000.

🛡️
$0 Lenders Mortgage Insurance

Avoid expensive LMI insurance premiums added to your loan balance.

🔄
Previous Homeowners Eligible

You can qualify even if you previously owned property before separation.

🏡
New & Established Homes

Buy an existing house, townhouse, unit, or house-and-land build.

🏛️
State Stamp Duty Waivers

Combine with state stamp duty exemptions to maximize total upfront savings.
2. Key Eligibility Criteria for the Family Home Guarantee

To qualify for the Family Home Guarantee, applicants must meet the following federal requirements: be an Australian citizen or permanent resident, be single (not married or in a de facto relationship), have at least one dependent child who is financially dependent on you, earn a taxable income under $125,000 in the previous financial year, and not currently own property in Australia at the time of settlement.
3. Eligible Property Types & Price Thresholds

You can use the 2% deposit guarantee to purchase an established home, a newly constructed townhouse, an off-the-plan apartment, or land combined with a comprehensive building contract. Price caps vary by state capital and regional territory (e.g., up to $950,000 in Greater Sydney and $800,000 in Greater Melbourne). EZ Mortgage Broker can verify your local suburb cap instantly.
4. Family Home Guarantee FAQs

Does child support count as assessable income for the loan?

Yes, many lenders on our panel accept court-ordered or Services Australia-registered child support payments as assessable income to boost your borrowing capacity, provided there is a consistent track record of payments.

Can I apply if I owned a house with an ex-partner in the past?

Yes. Unlike standard first home buyer grants, the Family Home Guarantee is specifically open to previous homeowners who currently do not hold title to any property.

title: Borrowing Power Decoded: How Australian Banks Actually Assess Your Capacity
author: R BAKSHI
summary: Why does one bank offer you $650,000 while another offers $800,000? Demystifying HEM benchmarks, interest rate buffers, and debt assessments.
body: Have you ever wondered why borrowing capacity estimates differ so wildly between lenders? A borrower who qualifies for $620,000 at one major bank might easily qualify for $780,000 at another lender on our panel. Understanding how Australian credit assessment algorithms evaluate your income, living expenses, and debts is the key to unlocking your maximum purchasing power.
1. The 3.00% APRA Serviceability Interest Rate Buffer

Under Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) guidelines, all authorized deposit-taking institutions (banks) must test your capacity to repay a mortgage at an interest rate 3.00% above the actual product rate. If your loan has an interest rate of 6.10%, the bank tests your monthly repayments at 9.10%. Non-bank lenders and specialist institutions sometimes utilize tailored serviceability buffers for specific refinancing and low-risk scenarios.

🛡️
APRA 3.00% Buffer

Tested repayment rates ensure safety margins against future rate hikes.

📊
HEM Living Expense Models

Declared expenses compared against statistical household benchmarks.

💳
Credit Card Multipliers

Card limits assessed at 3%–3.8% monthly repayment impact.

💼
Overtime & Bonus Shading

Banks shade variable allowances between 50% and 100%.

🏢
Rental Income Shading

Investment rents assessed at 70%–80% to allow for vacancies.

🎯
HECS / HELP Debt Rules

Student debt repayments calculated directly against gross income brackets.
2. Living Expenses & The Household Expenditure Measure (HEM)

When you lodge a home loan application, banks benchmark your declared monthly outgoings against the Household Expenditure Measure (HEM)—a statistical benchmark based on family size, location, and lifestyle. If your declared outgoings are lower than the HEM baseline, the bank automatically substitutes the higher HEM figure into their borrowing calculation.
3. Credit Card Limit Traps: The 3% Rule

A critical mistake many home buyers make is holding high unused credit card limits. Banks assess credit cards based on your total credit limit rather than your actual zero balance. A $15,000 unused credit card limit is assessed as an ongoing $450–$570 monthly debt commitment, which can reduce your overall borrowing power by up to $65,000. Reducing card limits prior to application immediately restores borrowing capacity.
4. Borrowing Capacity FAQs

How can I increase my borrowing capacity quickly?

Close unused credit cards, pay off minor buy-now-pay-later accounts, tidy up discretionary bank account spending for 3 months, and work with a broker who compares 50+ lender assessment calculators.

Does having HECS debt reduce borrowing power?

Yes. HECS/HELP repayments are deducted from your net monthly disposable income, which directly reduces serviceability. Some lenders evaluate HECS repayments more favorably than others.

title: Fixed vs Variable Home Loans: How to Choose in the Current Economic Cycle
author: R BAKSHI
summary: Split loans, 100% offset accounts, and redraw facilities compared: What Australian homeowners need to know about navigating RBA rate cycles.
body: Choosing between a fixed rate, a variable rate, or a hybrid split loan structure is one of the most critical financial decisions Australian property owners face. With Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) cash rate cycles impacting monthly budgets, understanding the benefits and trade-offs of each loan structure is essential to protect your household cash flow.
1. Fixed Rate Advantages & Hidden Constraints

A fixed interest rate locks your mortgage repayment amount for a set timeframe—typically 1, 2, 3, or 5 years. This provides complete certainty for family budgeting, insulating you against interest rate hikes. However, fixed rate loans usually limit additional repayments (typically capped at $10,000 to $20,000 per year) and do not support multiple 100% offset accounts.

🔒
Repayment Certainty

Lock your monthly repayment to make household budgeting 100% predictable.

📈
Hedge Against Rate Hikes

Shield your mortgage if the RBA increases the official cash rate.

⚡
100% Offset Accounts

Variable portions link to offset accounts to save interest on every dollar saved.

💸
Unlimited Extra Repayments

Variable loans allow you to pay down principal as aggressively as you wish.

⚖️
Split Loan Strategy

Combine fixed security with variable offset flexibility (e.g. 50/50 split).

🔄
Fee-Free Redraw

Access prepaid loan balances instantly whenever unexpected expenses arise.
2. The Power of 100% Offset Accounts on Variable Loans

On a variable mortgage, an offset account functions like an everyday transaction account that is linked directly to your loan balance. If you have a $600,000 mortgage at 6.00% and keep $50,000 sitting in your offset account, interest is calculated only on $550,000. Over the life of a 30-year mortgage, this saves tens of thousands of dollars in interest and cuts years off your loan term.
3. The Split Loan Hybrid Strategy

Many Australian homeowners choose the 'best of both worlds' by splitting their home loan. For example, fixing 60% of your borrowing provides peace of mind that the majority of your repayment will never change, while keeping 40% variable allows you to link your salary and emergency savings to an offset account for maximum interest savings.
4. Fixed vs Variable FAQs

What are break costs on a fixed rate loan?

If you sell your home, refinance, or pay off a fixed loan early, the bank may charge economic break costs based on wholesale money market movements. Always consult your broker before breaking a fixed term.

Can I split my loan into multiple portions?

Yes. Most lenders allow you to split your mortgage into two or more accounts (e.g., 50% fixed and 50% variable) with zero extra setup cost.

title: SMSF Property Lending: How to Buy Residential & Commercial Real Estate Through Super
author: R BAKSHI
summary: Leverage your superannuation balance to purchase investment property using Limited Recourse Borrowing Arrangements (LRBA).
body: Self-Managed Super Funds (SMSFs) allow Australians to take direct control over their retirement wealth by investing in physical residential real estate or commercial property. By combining member balances and directing employer super guarantee contributions into an SMSF property loan, investors can build substantial tax-sheltered equity for retirement.
1. Understanding Limited Recourse Borrowing Arrangements (LRBA)

When an SMSF borrows to purchase property, Australian superannuation law requires the loan to be structured as a Limited Recourse Borrowing Arrangement (LRBA). Under this legal framework, a separate Bare Trust (or Security Trust) holds legal title to the property until the loan is fully repaid, shielding all other assets within your super fund from lender recourse in the unlikely event of default.

Core LRBA FeatureSuper Law FrameworkKey Investor Benefit
🛡️ Limited Recourse ProtectionSection 67A SIS Act 1993Lenders have zero claim over your super fund's shares, cash, or other assets in default.
🏢 Commercial Business Real PropertyATO Arm's Length RulesOwn your business premises and pay 100% tax-deductible rent directly to your own super fund.
💰 15% Concessional Tax RateAccumulation Phase TaxRental income taxed at just 15% during accumulation, dropping to 0% in pension phase.
📉 Capital Gains Tax DiscountsSuper CGT ProvisionsCapital gains tax is discounted to 10% on assets held >12 months (0% in retirement).
🤝 Pool Family Super BalancesUp to 6 Fund MembersCombine super balances of spouses or family members to acquire high-value property.
🏗️ Single Acquirable AssetStandalone Title RuleSpecialist single-part contract structures available for NDIS, residential, and commercial.

📋 Essential SMSF Property Investment Checklist

  • SMSF Trust Deed: Must explicitly permit borrowing under Section 67A LRBA provisions.
  • Bare Trust & Corporate Trustee: Separate legal entity established before signing property contracts.
  • Minimum Liquidity Buffer: Lenders require 5%–10% in liquid cash/shares retained post-settlement.
  • Sole Purpose Test: Residential property cannot be leased to, lived in, or used by fund members or relatives.
2. Buying Commercial Property for Your Operating Business

One of the most popular strategies for Australian business owners is purchasing their commercial warehouse, medical clinic, or office through their SMSF. Under ATO rules, business real property can be leased directly to your own operating business at fair market commercial rates. Your business claims 100% tax deductions on lease payments, while your SMSF receives the rent taxed at just 15%, transforming an overhead expense into wealth.

Lending ParameterResidential SMSF LoanCommercial SMSF Loan
Maximum LVR70% – 80% LVR70% – 75% LVR
Minimum Fund Balance$250,000 – $350,000 combined$250,000+
Tenant RulesStrictly unrelated arm's-length tenantsCan be leased to own operating business
Repayment StructurePrincipal & Interest or 5-yr Interest-OnlyPrincipal & Interest or Interest-Only
3. SMSF Residential Lending Guidelines & LVR Caps

For residential SMSF property purchases, specialist lenders typically require a 20% to 30% deposit (70%–80% LVR maximum), a minimum combined fund balance of $250k–$350k, and 5%–10% in liquid post-settlement buffers. Fund members and their relatives are strictly prohibited from living in, holidaying at, or leasing residential properties held within the SMSF.
4. SMSF Property Lending FAQs

Can my SMSF borrow to renovate an existing property?

Under LRBA rules, borrowed funds can only be used to maintain or repair a property to its original condition. Substantial improvements or structural changes must be funded entirely from existing super cash reserves.

Which lenders provide SMSF home loans in Australia?

While major four banks withdrew from SMSF retail lending, specialist lenders on our panel (e.g. La Trobe, Firstmac, Thinktank, Macquarie Commercial) offer competitive SMSF residential and commercial loans.

title: Property Investment Structuring: Equity Release, Cross-Collateralisation & Interest-Only
author: R BAKSHI
summary: Smart loan structuring is what separates successful multi-property investors from those who get stuck after their first purchase.
body: Smart loan structuring is what separates successful multi-property investors from those who find their borrowing capacity blocked after just one purchase. When building a scalable property portfolio in Australia, how you set up your loan accounts, manage equity release, and avoid lender traps like cross-collateralisation matters just as much as the properties you buy.
1. Releasing Usable Equity via Standalone Top-Up Facilities

If your home has increased in value, you can unlock usable equity up to 80% LVR without selling. The golden rule of portfolio finance is to structure this released equity as a standalone investment top-up facility or line of credit rather than mixing funds directly with your owner-occupied mortgage. This ensures that 100% of the interest on the top-up loan remains fully tax-deductible against your investment property income.

  • Rule 2: Keep 100% offset accounts attached to non-deductible home debt first.
  • Rule 3: Never cross-collateralise properties with the same lender.
2. The Dangers of Cross-Collateralisation (And How to Avoid It)

Cross-collateralisation occurs when a bank uses one mortgage to secure multiple properties (e.g. your family home and your investment property together). When cross-collateralised, you cannot sell one property without the bank dictating how much proceeds must go toward paying down your other debt, and an unfavorable valuation on one property can freeze equity across your entire portfolio. We structure all investor loans on un-crossed, standalone titles.
3. Principal & Interest vs Interest-Only for Investors

While paying Principal & Interest (P&I) builds equity, many investors choose 5-year Interest-Only (IO) terms on their investment loans. This minimizes non-deductible holding costs, allowing you to direct all spare cash flow into the 100% offset account of your owner-occupied home loan to eliminate non-deductible personal debt first.
4. Investment Structuring FAQs

How is usable equity calculated on my home?

Usable Equity = (Property Valuation × 80%) − Existing Mortgage Balance. For example, on a $900,000 home with a $400,000 loan, your usable equity is ($720,000 − $400,000) = $320,000.

Can I buy an investment property in a family trust?

Yes. Discretionary Family Trusts with corporate trustees offer asset protection and flexible distribution of rental income, supported by specialist trust lenders on our panel.
